keyword: treasury take over federal student loans
claims: The U.S. Department of the Treasury is taking over management of federal student loans in a multi-phase transition from the Department of Education.
Initial efforts focus on transitioning roughly 9 million defaulted accounts to the U.S. Department of the Treasury for collections and repayment support.
The initial phase was announced in March 2026.
The initial phase involves moving ~$180 billion in student loans that are in default (over 270 days behind) to the U.S. Department of the Treasury.
The U.S. Department of the Treasury will eventually take over the entire ~$1.7 trillion federal student loan portfolio.
The move is part of the Trump administration’s initiative to shrink the Education Department and centralize debt collection.
The move utilizes the Treasury's ability to manage, collect, and potentially garnish wages through the IRS for delinquent borrowers.
According to Business Insider, most borrowers should continue making payments through their current federal servicer until instructed otherwise.
The U.S. Department of the Treasury will take over collections focusing on bringing defaulted borrowers back into good standing.
Defaulted borrowers will see their debt management moved from Federal Student Aid (FSA) to the U.S. Department of the Treasury.
The transition was officially announced to start in March 2026, as reported by NPR and AP News.
